label: Pampanga's at-large congressional district
title: Pampanga's at-large congressional district
wikitext:
{{short description|Former congressional district in the Philippines}} '''Pampanga's at-large congressional district''' was the provincewide [[electoral district]] used to elect members of [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|Philippine national legislatures]] in [[Pampanga]] before 1987.{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=September 6, 2025 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} Pampanga was initially composed of one representative district, wherein it elected four representatives, at large, to the [[Malolos Congress]] in [[1898 Philippine legislative election|1898]]. It was later divided into two representative districts in 1907 for the [[Philippine Assembly]];{{cite PH act|chamber=Act|number=1582|date=January 9, 1907|url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l5054|title=An Act to Provide for the Holding of Elections in the Philippine Islands, for the Organization of the Philippine Assembly, and for Other Purposes|accessdate=September 6, 2025}} it remained so until 1941. In the disruption caused by the [[World War II|Second World War]], Pampanga was represented by [[#1943–1944|two delegates]] in the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the [[Governor of Pampanga|provincial governor]] (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a citywide assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]].{{cite web |url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1943-constitution/ |title=The 1943 Constitution |publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]] |accessdate=December 18, 2025 |archive-date=June 2, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200602190153/https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1943-constitution/ |url-status=dead }} Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, Pampanga's pre-war two-district representation was retained; this remained so until 1972. The province and the chartered city of Angeles were represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region III]] from 1978 to 1984, and together elected [[Regular Batasang Pambansa#Members|four representatives]] at-large to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] from 1984 to 1986.{{cite web|url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l829a |title=Batas Pambansa Blg. 643, (1983-12-21) |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate=December 18, 2025}} Pampanga (with the highly urbanized city of Angeles) was redistricted into four [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional districts]] under the new Constitution{{Cite web|url=http://www.lawphil.net/consti/cons1987.html|title = 1987 Philippine Constitution - the LawPhil Project}} which took effect on February 7, 1987, and elected members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]].{{cite web|url=https://chanrobles.com/region3.htm |title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=December 18, 2025}} ==Representation history==
